name: Nigerian Meat Pie
summary: Flaky, buttery pastry parcels filled with peppery minced beef, potato and carrot, baked until golden.
story: Meat pie is a staple of Nigerian bakeries and is sold at roadside stalls, school gates and events. It is a favourite in lunchboxes and at birthday parties, often eaten warm with a cold drink.

items.name: egg yolk
items.note: beaten with 1 tbsp milk for glazing

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour, salt and baking powder with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs with a few pea-sized lumps. Add the iced water a tablespoon at a time and bring it together into a soft dough without kneading. It should hold when squeezed but not feel sticky.

steps.title: Chill the dough
steps.text: Flatten the dough into a disc, wrap it and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Cold butter is what gives the flaky layers, so do not skip this.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the onion for 3 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the beef, breaking up lumps, and cook for 6-8 minutes until no pink remains and the liquid has evaporated. Stir in the curry powder, thyme, crumbled stock cube and scotch bonnet.

steps.title: Simmer the filling
steps.text: Add the potatoes and carrots, sprinkle over the tablespoon of flour and stir for a minute. Pour in the stock, cover and simmer for 12-15 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the mixture is thick and almost dry. Taste and adjust salt, then cool completely.

steps.title: Cut the rounds
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 C (400 F). Roll the dough about 3 mm thick on a floured surface and cut circles of about 12 cm. Re-roll the offcuts once only.

steps.title: Fill and seal
steps.text: Put 2 heaped tablespoons of cooled filling on one half of each circle, leaving a clear border. Brush the edge with water, fold over and press shut, then crimp with a fork. A hot filling would melt the butter, so make sure it is cold.

steps.title: Glaze and bake
steps.text: Place the pies on a lined tray, brush with the egg yolk mixture and prick the tops once with a fork. Bake for 25-30 minutes until deep golden and firm to the touch.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Let the pies cool on a rack for 10 minutes so the filling settles. Serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Dice the potato and carrot tiny, about 5 mm, so the filling packs neatly and cooks through.
Keep the filling fairly dry; a wet filling makes soggy bottoms and splits the pastry.
Pies freeze well unbaked; bake from frozen adding 8-10 minutes.
Cold butter and quick handling are the secret to a flaky crust.

swaps.swap: Use habanero or half a red chilli; the heat is similar but the fruity flavour is slightly different.
Minced chicken or turkey works and gives a lighter pie; add a little extra oil as it is leaner.
